# Ben Green's Open Problem 63

Let $A$ be the smallest set containing $2$ and $3$ and such that $a_1a_2 - 1 \in A$
if $a_1, a_2 \in A$. Does $A$ have positive density?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
- [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»`.
-/

@[expose] public section

findings.description: The redirect silently chooses the distinct-input version of the problem. Lines 24–25, following Green's displayed statement, describe closure under a₁a₂ − 1 without requiring a₁ ≠ a₂. However, the imported Erdos424.nextGeneration explicitly requires x ≠ y. These constructions give different sets: the unrestricted closure contains 8 = 3·3 − 1, whereas Erdos424.generatedSet never contains 8; both facts were proved in the scratch file. This is a source ambiguity rather than a confirmed error in the imported theorem: Green's comments identify OEIS A005244 and Erdős 424, and the original Erdős reference explicitly requires distinct elements. The set-level counterexample alone does not establish that the two density questions are inequivalent.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 63, pp. 30–31, https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf: “such that a₁a₂ − 1 ∈ A if a₁, a₂ ∈ A”; its comments identify A005244 and Erdős Problem 424. In contrast, Erdős, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory, III (1977), p. 71, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf, says “Form all products of two distinct elements of the sequence”. https://www.erdosproblems.com/424 likewise specifies i ≠ j.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly document that the redirect follows the distinct-input interpretation supported by Green's references, while Green's displayed wording omits that restriction. If the literal unrestricted version is intended, add a separate Green 63 variant using a generation rule without x ≠ y. Keep the canonical Erdős definition unchanged, since it matches its primary source.

reformulations.difference: The imported definition uses the union of cumulative finite-generation stages rather than directly specifying the least set containing 2 and 3 and closed under the distinct-input operation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The stages are increasing. Two elements appearing at different stages both belong to the stage indexed by the maximum of those indices, so their permitted product-minus-one appears at the next stage. Conversely, induction shows that every stage lies in any set containing the seeds and closed under the operation. A Lean equivalence with the least-set characterization was proved. This concerns the distinct-input formulation, not an equivalence with Green's literal unrestricted wording.

reformulations.difference: The imported theorem expresses the source's eventual linear counting bound through positive lowerDensity, whose partial densities count elements below N rather than elements in [1,N].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The ratios are bounded between 0 and 1. Their liminf is positive exactly when some positive constant is an eventual lower bound. Multiplication by N gives the counting formulation; changing the endpoint convention preserves an eventual positive linear bound. The scratch file proves, for every S ⊆ ℕ with 0 ∉ S, the equivalence between 0 < S.lowerDensity and existence of c > 0 such that eventually c*N ≤ |S ∩ [1,N]|. It also proves that generatedSet contains no zero.

could_not_verify: file: Whether the positive-density questions for the literal unrestricted Green closure and the distinct-input Erdős closure are mathematically equivalent. Their generating sets differ, but that alone does not settle equivalence of their density properties.
review.notes: The reviewed file has no local mathematical declarations, answer slots, or status attributes; it is entirely a redirect. The imported definitions and both density statements were checked. The canonical distinct-input formulation agrees with the original Erdős source and OEIS. Its exact-density variant explicitly asks for a positive natural-density limit and does not purport to be equivalent to positive lower density. The Erdős page still records OPEN with proof claims, consistent with the imported metadata despite Korsky's announced proof. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully: checks include the least-set characterization, density equivalence, exclusion of 0 and 1, the witness 8, and finite computations matching OEIS through 250. The validation proofs do not depend on sorryAx. No repository files were edited.
